taste.name: Accent-at-Interaction-Only
taste.trigger: A third brand color (#BFD55D) was approved for use, but it measures 1.48:1 against the cream background — unreadable as a resting fill or text color
taste.decision: Confined it entirely to moments the visitor causes (hover fills, a flip-revealed border) over using it anywhere in the page's idle state
taste.reason: A color that only appears because you did something reads as feedback, not decoration — it confirms the action registered without asking anyone to read text on a 1.48:1 background
evidence: 0% static-area presence for #BFD55D in the DOM color sample
token exists in global.css but never surfaces at rest

taste.name: Two-Radius System
taste.trigger: Needing to distinguish "this is a container" from "this is an action" across dozens of repeated components
taste.decision: Every rounded corner is exactly 16px or a full pill over a graduated radius scale
taste.reason: Two shapes are enough vocabulary to be instantly legible without thinking; a third intermediate radius asks the eye to classify a distinction nobody needs
evidence: effects.radii: 16px (9×) and pill/9999px (6×) are the only two values site-wide

taste.name: Single Weight Pair
taste.trigger: A page with 6 distinct font sizes already had hierarchy machinery available from size alone
taste.decision: Exactly two font weights (400, 600) over a fuller ladder that would let size, weight, and color all carry hierarchy independently
taste.reason: Stacking weight variation on an already-wide size range multiplies how many "looks" a reader parses as meaningfully different; two weights keeps emphasis legible at a glance
evidence: weightDistribution: 400 (24×) everywhere; 600 (9×) used only for the 3 uppercase eyebrow labels

taste.name: Alignment as Mode-Switch
taste.trigger: The page mixes two reading modes — "receive one statement" (hero) and "compare three things" (audience cards)
taste.decision: Center-aligned every full-bleed singular block over left-aligning everything inside a bounded card, rather than one alignment site-wide
taste.reason: Centering signals "just read this"; left-alignment signals "this is a list item, compare it to its neighbors" — alignment tells the visitor which mode to switch into before reading a word
